candidates.definition: the pair (d, N) in the lexicographic order, with N the number of terms of in(G), the initial form of the residual factor G.
d/q, the residual order divided by q. Along one walk q does not change, so this candidate fails exactly at the kangaroo points.
d - p^rF, with rF the r of Moh: the largest r such that in(F) is a p^r-th power.
d - p^rG, with rG the largest r such that in(G) is a p^r-th power (rG = 0 when d = 0).
the pair (d, -rF) in the lexicographic order, with rF the r of Moh.
the one-step bound d' <= floor(d/p^rF) p^rF + p^rF that the proof of Moh uses (Hauser-Perlega, Section 3). This is a bound, not a value that goes down.
